concepts.def: The position an organism occupies in a food chain. Trophic levels can be represented by numbers, starting at level 1 with plants and algae; further trophic levels are numbered subsequently according to how far the organism is along the food chain.
An organism at trophic level 1. Plants and algae make their own food and are called producers.
An organism at trophic level 2. Herbivores eat plants/algae and are called primary consumers.
An organism at trophic level 3. Carnivores that eat herbivores are called secondary consumers.
An organism at trophic level 4. Carnivores that eat other carnivores are called tertiary consumers.
A carnivore with no predators. Apex predators are found at the end of a food chain.
A microorganism that breaks down dead plant and animal matter by secreting enzymes into the environment. Small soluble food molecules then diffuse into the microorganism.

A diagram constructed to represent the relative amount of biomass in each level of a food chain. Trophic level 1 is at the bottom of the pyramid, and the width of each bar represents the biomass at that level.

concepts.term: Transfer of light energy by producers
concepts.def: Producers are mostly plants and algae which transfer about 1% of the incident energy from light for photosynthesis.
Only approximately 10% of the biomass from each trophic level is transferred to the level above it, so less biomass is available at each higher trophic level.

Biomass is lost between trophic levels because not all the ingested material is absorbed, some being egested as faeces, and because some absorbed material is lost as waste, such as carbon dioxide and water in respiration and water and urea in urine. Large amounts of glucose are used in respiration.

The biomass transferred to a trophic level expressed as a percentage or fraction of the biomass available at the level below it: biomass transferred divided by biomass available, multiplied by 100 for a percentage.

mcqs.q: A food chain is: algae to mayfly larvae to minnow to pike. The pike has no predators in this ecosystem. Which statement about this food chain is correct?
options: The pike is a tertiary consumer.
The minnow is an apex predator.
The mayfly larvae are at level 1.
The pike is a secondary consumer.
mcqs.explain: The pike is a carnivore that eats another carnivore, the minnow, so it is at trophic level 4 and is called a tertiary consumer. As it has no predators it is also an apex predator.

mcqs.q: An oak tree of biomass 4000 kg supports 3000 caterpillars of total biomass 6 kg, which are eaten by 20 blue tits of total biomass 0.2 kg. Which description of the pyramid of biomass for these data is correct?
options: The oak tree is the widest bar, at the bottom.
The three bars are drawn with equal widths.
The oak tree is the narrowest bar, at the bottom.
The caterpillars form the bottom bar, as level 1.
mcqs.explain: Trophic level 1 is at the bottom of the pyramid, and the bars represent the relative amount of biomass in each level, so the oak tree with 4000 kg forms the widest bar.

mcqs.q: Approximately what percentage of the incident energy from light do producers transfer for photosynthesis?
options: About 10%
About 1%
About 50%
About 90%
mcqs.explain: Producers are mostly plants and algae which transfer about 1% of the incident energy from light for photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: A trophic level contains 6000 g of biomass. Approximately what mass of biomass is transferred to the trophic level above it?
mcqs.explain: Only approximately 10% of the biomass from each trophic level is transferred to the level above it, and 10% of 6000 g is 600 g.

mcqs.q: Which statement explains why biomass is lost between one trophic level and the next?
options: The uneaten parts of the prey are the main loss.
Glucose used in respiration is passed on.
Much of the glucose is used in respiration.
Producers use 10% of the light energy.
mcqs.explain: Large amounts of glucose are used in respiration, and the carbon dioxide and water produced are lost as waste, so this material is not transferred to the trophic level above.

mcqs.q: A trophic level contains 800 g of biomass. The trophic level above it contains 40 g of biomass. What is the efficiency of the biomass transfer between these two levels?
mcqs.explain: The efficiency is the biomass transferred as a percentage of the mass available: 40 divided by 800, multiplied by 100, gives 5%.

mcqs.q: A food chain is: grass to rabbits to foxes. Which statement about this food chain is correct?
options: Similar numbers of rabbits and foxes live here.
Far fewer foxes than rabbits are supported.
More foxes than rabbits live here, as foxes hunt.
Nearly all the rabbits' biomass reaches foxes.
mcqs.explain: Only approximately 10% of the biomass from each trophic level is transferred to the level above it, so much less biomass is available to the foxes and fewer organisms can be supported at that level.
